A B S T R A C T
The microstructure and mechanical properties of Fe-35Mn-xAl-0.1C (x = 4, 6, 8, 10) low-density steels were
studied using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and tensile machine.
It is found that the microstructure evolves with the increasing of Al content from a single austenite phase steel for
4 %Al, to a ferrite-based duplex steel for 8 %Al, but nearly a fully ferrite phase steel with 10 %Al. As the Al
content is increased from 4 wt % to 8 wt %, the yield strength and tensile strength are significantly increased
from 239 MPa to 552 MPa–455 MPa and 740 MPa, respectively, while the uniform elongation is only slightly
decreased from 38.5 % to 31.0 %. However, as the Al content is increased up to 10 %, the yield strength is
gradually increased to 585 MPa, but the tensile elongation is sharply decreased down to about 4.6 %. Based on
the thorough microstructure examination of the dislocation type and dislocation pattern and the microstructure
evolution during tensile deformation, it is concluded that the excellent combination of the mechanical property
of the 8Al steel is realized by the activation of the edge-typed dislocation and dynamic slip band refinement in
the ferrite grain mitigated by the surrounded austenite grains, which enhanced the strain hardening rate
significantly. This study not only reveals a new ductility-enhancing mechanism of ferrite + austenite duplex
steel, but also provides a new route for designing BCC based low-density steel with high strength and high
ductility.

The research on duplex low-density steels primarily focused on
austenite-based duplex low-density steels [23–25]. The introduction of

ordered phases into high-aluminum ferrite can bring a
significant enhancement in yield strength, but simultaneously lead to an
increase in brittleness [15,23,24,26,27]. It was found that B2 and DO3
ordered domains appear in Fe-Al alloys during the cooling process when

dislocation deformation characteristics of ferrite will be significantly
influenced by the interactions between dislocations and ordered phases.
However, the systematic work in this aspect has not yet been conducted
to investigate the work hardening mechanisms of high-aluminum
ferritic matrix-based lightweight steels.
To address this issue of both dislocation patterns and work hardening
behaviors, Fe35MnxAl0.1C (x = 4, 6, 8, 10 wt%) low-density steels were
designed. Among them, Fe35Mn4Al0.1C is an austenitic lightweight
steel, Fe35Mn6Al0.1C is an austenite based duplex lightweight steel,
and Fe35Mn8Al0.1C and Fe35Mn10Al0.1C are ferrite based duplex
lightweight steels. Tensile deformations were carried out to reveal the
microstructural effects on the work hardening behaviors and mechanical
properties of the designed steels. And both scanning electron microscope
(SEM) and transmission electron microscope (TEM) were applied to
reveal the microstructure evolution in terms of dislocation patterns of
the designed steel during deformation process. The effects of micro
structure on the dislocation type, dislocation pattern, work hardening
behavior and mechanical property will be discussed, which is expected
to give a thorough understanding on the evolution of dislocation pattern
and the work hardening behavior of the ferrite-based duplex lightweight
steel.
